newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Tuesday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at an intra-day low of 19,430 yuan ($2,342) per tonne, rising 70 yuan. It opened at 19,480 and hit a high of 19,490.
November was the only loser, falling 20 to 18,950.
December rose 100 to 19,200, January 70 to 19,420, March 60 to 19,440, April 40 to 19,400 and May 70 to 19,460.
Copper opened up and profit-taking pushed the prices to close off their highs but still higher from Monday's close.
Traders said the LME gains boosted the confidence of long position holders but copper met strong selling pressure at high levels due to sufficient supplies of domestic spot copper.

"Many investors were willing to offset their long positions at the 19,500 yuan level with easy spot copper," a trader said. "Others preferred to stay on the sidelines given the uncertain short-term market trend."
Traders said the LME was the most important factor on a lack of domestic market-moving news and Shanghai copper would fall if the LME could not keep an upward trend in the short term.
"Successive falls of the LME's stockpiles has boosted the morale of long position holders," a second trader said. "The short-term trend in Shanghai will depend on the LME movements."
Analysts expected copper to continue to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
November Aluminium closed unchanged at 13,450, December did not trade and January rose 200 to 13,600.
Total volume fell to 620 tonnes from 1,080. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
